class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Define the sine integral: I_n from zero to pi/2.",
            "Observe the area shrinking as n increases.",
            "Use the reduction formula: I_n equals (n-1)/n I_{n-2}.",
            "Compare even and odd powers for insight.",
            "This formula reveals pi's structure through sine."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Reduction Formula for Sine", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define equations
        formula = MathTex(
            r"I_n = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^n(x) \, dx",
            r"I_n = \frac{n-1}{n} I_{n-2}",
            tex_template=TexTemplate()
        )
        formula[0].set_color("#33FF57")
        formula[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(formula[0], "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula[0]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Simple illustration of shrinking area
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, PI/2, 0.5], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x)**2, color=BLUE)
        area = axes.get_area(curve, [0, PI/2], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, curve, area), "D2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(area))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(area))
        self.place_at_grid(formula[1], "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula[1]))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(formula[1][0][2:5], color="#FFFF33")
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Evaluate the ratio I_{2n+1} over I_{2n}.", "As n grows, this ratio approaches one.", "Balance the integral products to isolate pi.", "The tug-of-war reveals pi/2.", "Algebraic manipulation bridges integrals to pi."]
        self.setup_layout("Deriving the Ratio", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        ratio_expr = MathTex(r"{{I_{2n+1}}} \over {{I_{2n}}}", color=WHITE)
        ratio_highlight = MathTex(r"{{I_{2n+1}}} \over {{I_{2n}}}", color="#3357FF")
        
        term_rel = MathTex(r"\text{Relationship: } n \to \infty \implies 1", color="#FF33FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(ratio_expr, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3357FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Transform(ratio_expr, ratio_highlight))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF33FF")
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(term_rel, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        balance_label = Text("Tug-of-War Balance", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(balance_label, 'A4')))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(ORANGE)
        res_pi = MathTex(r"\pi/2", color=ORANGE)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(res_pi, 'E5', scale_factor=2)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Wallis Product Formula", [
            "The Wallis Product defines pi/2 as a product.",
            "Alternating fractions build the target value.",
            "Each ingredient improves the flavor meter's precision.",
            "Convergence shows pi emerging from simple ratios.",
            "The infinite product mirrors the circle's nature."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        wallis_formula = MathTex(
            r"\frac{\pi}{2} = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} \left( \frac{2n}{2n-1} \cdot \frac{2n}{2n+1} \right)",
            color="#57FFFF"
        )
        self.place_in_area(wallis_formula, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(wallis_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#57FFFF")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        factors = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"\left( \frac{2}{1} \cdot \frac{2}{3} \right)"),
            MathTex(r"\left( \frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{4}{5} \right)"),
            MathTex(r"\left( \frac{6}{5} \cdot \frac{6}{7} \right)")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(factors, "C2", "C5")
        
        for factor in factors:
            self.play(FadeIn(factor))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        flavor_meter = Rectangle(width=4, height=0.5, color=WHITE).next_to(factors, DOWN, buff=1)
        self.place_at_grid(flavor_meter, "E3")
        label = Text("Flavor Meter", font_size=20).next_to(flavor_meter, UP)
        self.add(flavor_meter, label)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF57FF")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        final_formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\pi}{2}", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(final_formula, "D3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(factors), FadeOut(flavor_meter), FadeOut(label), ReplacementTransform(wallis_formula, final_formula))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Intuition", [
            "Simple integer ratios reconstruct transcendental constants.",
            "Convergence maps the journey to pi.",
            "Fractal adjustments refine our mathematical reach."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#87CEEB")
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(circle))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF7F50")
        
        # Illustrate convergence/infinite factors
        factors = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 6):
            frac = MathTex(r"\frac{" + str(2*i) + "}{" + str(2*i-1) + "}", font_size=24)
            factors.add(frac)
        factors.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(factors, 'E1', 'E6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(factors))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        result = MathTex(r"\frac{\pi}{2} \approx \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{2n}{2n-1} \cdot \frac{2n}{2n+1}", font_size=32, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'B3')
        self.play(Write(result))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Wallis Product: Unveiling Pi through Infinite Ratios

sections.title: Introduction: The Quest for Pi
sections.content: Hook the audience by moving beyond geometry. Contrast the familiar circle formula with an infinite process. Briefly introduce the concept of 'Infinite Products' as the multiplication equivalent of infinite series.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Pixel-Art' circle that becomes smoother as we add more data points, leading to a ratio of integers.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Reduction Formula for Sine
sections.content: Establish the foundation by defining the integral I_n = ∫[0 to π/2] sin^n(x) dx. Show the reduction formula I_n = ((n-1)/n) * I_{n-2}. Explain that this provides a way to express π by comparing even and odd powers of sine.
sections.example: An animation showing the area under sin^n(x) shrinking and becoming 'boxier' as n increases.

sections.title: Deriving the Ratio
sections.content: Evaluate the ratio I_{2n+1} / I_{2n}. Demonstrate that as n approaches infinity, this ratio approaches 1. By substituting the reduction formula results, we isolate π on one side of the equation.
sections.example: A 'Tug-of-War' animation where two side-by-side expressions (the odd and even integral products) balance out to π/2.

sections.title: The Wallis Product Formula
sections.content: Present the final identity: π/2 = (2/1 * 2/3) * (4/3 * 4/5) * (6/5 * 6/7)... highlight the alternating nature of the sequence.
sections.example: A 'Robot Chef' adding fractions to a pot; as the chef adds more ingredients following the pattern, the 'Flavor Meter' converges toward the value of π/2.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize how simple ratios of integers can reconstruct a transcendental number. Relate this to the concept of convergence.
sections.example: A final visual of a fractal-like progression where smaller and smaller integer adjustments refine the precision of the circle's circumference calculation.
